exam_scheme.note: DSSSB conducts teacher recruitment under One-Tier Teaching (I-T-T) examination scheme comprising a single 2-hour CBT paper of 200 MCQs (200 marks). Candidates must qualify in Section B (domain pedagogical and subject paper) with prescribed category-wise minimum qualifying marks, while final selection is strictly prepared on aggregate marks of Section A and Section B combined.

financial_package.note: Government school teachers in Delhi are placed under 7th CPC Central Pay Scales: Trained Graduate Teachers commence at Pay Level 7 (entry basic ₹44,900) while Assistant Teachers (Primary / PRT) commence at Pay Level 6 (entry basic ₹35,400). Both cadres receive Delhi Class 'X' metro allowances and central benefits.
financial_package.pay_source_label: DSSSB Advt No. 02/2024 — Pay Scale for TGTs (₹44,900 – ₹1,42,400, Pay Level 7)
financial_package.estimate_note: Spans entry PRT at Level 6 basic ₹35,400 (gross ~₹72,240, in-hand ~₹66,600) to TGT at Level 7 basic ₹44,900 (gross ~₹90,100, in-hand ~₹83,000) with 58% DA, 30% Delhi HRA, ₹3,600 + DA on TA, less 10% NPS and DGEHS deduction.
official_perks: Delhi Government Employees Health Scheme (DGEHS) comprehensive cashless medical coverage across empanelled private and state hospitals
Summer Vacation (approx. 50 days) and Winter Break (approx. 10 days) with full salary entitlement
Child Care Leave (CCL) up to 730 days for eligible female teachers
Children Education Allowance (CEA) of ₹2,250 per month per child plus hostel subsidy
National Pension System (NPS) with 14% defined government monthly contribution
Continuous professional development and state/national awards through SCERT Delhi

competition_benchmarks.note: DSSSB teacher examinations are among Delhi's most competitive government recruitments. In the 2024 Combined Examination for TGTs (Advt No. 02/2024), 5,118 vacancies were advertised across disciplines. In TGT Mathematics alone (Post Code 803/24), 25,276 candidates appeared in CBT for 1,119 vacancies, and in TGT Social Science (Post Code 805/24), 26,945 candidates appeared for 310 vacancies, verified directly from DSSSB's official marks notices.
